findings.title: Call to non-existent zero-argument method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate()` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only such method defined in the parent class `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` which requires a `UserModel` parameter. There is no zero-argument overload anywhere in the class hierarchy shown. This will cause a compilation error.

findings.title: WebAuthn conditional UI no longer initialized on first login (user == null)
findings.body: The `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` method requires `user != null` to return true. In `authenticate()`, when the user has not yet been identified (first login), `context.getUser()` is null, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns false and `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never called. Previously, WebAuthn setup was performed inside the `else` branch (user == null). This means the WebAuthn conditional UI (autocomplete passkey) will not be available on the initial login page, breaking first-time passkey login. The same issue affects the `challenge(context, error, field)` override at line 137, where error pages during first login will also lack WebAuthn setup.

findings.title: WebAuthn not re-initialized on error during first login attempt
findings.body: The overridden `challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext context, String error, String field)` method now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` which requires a non-null user. During a first login attempt with an invalid username, `context.getUser()` will be null (the user lookup failed), so WebAuthn conditional UI attributes will not be set on the error page. The original code explicitly checked `context.getUser() == null` to handle this case. Users who mistype their username on the first login will lose the ability to use passkeys on the error page.

findings.title: Missing @Override annotation on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators
findings.body: The method `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` overrides the method introduced in `WebAuthnAuthenticator` but lacks the `@Override` annotation. While not a bug, this makes it harder for the compiler to detect if the parent method signature changes, and is inconsistent with the `fillContextForm` override on line 42 which does have `@Override`.
